_: German fixture content, kept out of the generator so that device/tools/make_fixtures.mjs stays English like the rest of the code. The same arrangement exchange/fixtures/source/labels.de.json has, for the same reason. Real set names are German, and a name rule about UTF-8 has to be exercised on text that actually ships rather than on an ASCII stand-in.
_sentences: Whole sentences, for the package fixtures. A key on a talker says a sentence rather than a word, and the package carries it twice - as the label any other editor shows and as the vocalization the device speaks - so the fixtures need text that is a sentence.
_joining: The joining game, which is what layout.bin version 3 is for: a set key shows a tile split down the diagonal with the two halves of a compound word on it and says them out loud, and one of the four speech keys carries the word those halves make. Two rounds' worth of words, because a single round cannot show a key going anywhere - and two more set names after them, because a chain that comes back round to where it started needs more rounds than it has ends.
_collections: What a collection is called in the device's own menu, which is the name of its first set - the format carries no name for a collection and collectionHeadName() in firmware/vorlaut/collections.h is where that is argued. Their own group because of what is asked of them: nine characters a line and two lines, so these are the names that have to survive being wrapped and cut.
_wrapped: The same names as a key really shows them: nine glyphs a line and two lines, broken at spaces. The pairs live here rather than in the generator for the reason every other string does - one of them carries an umlaut, and quoting a fragment of German inside an English file is what tests/test_language.py is there to catch. They are written out and never computed: a fixture that worked its own expectation out would agree with whatever it worked it out with.
